video_title: The Crypto Train Has Left the Station with Lighter
gist: Recorded at Token 2049, Lighter founder Vlad explains how finance-specific ZK circuits (~1% the cost of general-purpose ZK compute) enable a low-latency, verifiable on-chain order book, why Lighter copied Robinhood's zero-fee retail model, and how its points program (near-100% testnet-to-mainnet conversion) was designed against wash trading. He bets most of finance moves on-chain (100x growth), with near-term priorities of options, RWA liquidity and a CFTC license.

insights.claim: Lighter uses ZK circuits customized for financial primitives rather than general-purpose ZK computation, which Vlad says lets it run financial primitives at about 1% of the cost of a general-purpose ZK computer.
insights.speaker: Vlad (Lighter founder)
insights.so_what: Application-specific ZK circuits may be a structural cost moat versus general-purpose zkVM/rollup exchanges.
insights.quote: we can actually run finance you know financial primitives at like 1% of the cost of running a general purpose computer

insights.claim: Vlad frames Lighter's custom ZK circuits as analogous to Nvidia chips specialized for AI operations: specialization of the proving stack for finance is the core innovation.
insights.speaker: Vlad (Lighter founder)
insights.so_what: Expect vertical specialization (finance-specific provers) to beat generic infrastructure on cost/latency.
insights.quote: how like Nvidia chips are customized for specific operations in AI it's like we have ZK circuits that are customized for um you know for for finance

insights.claim: The founders seriously considered three crypto/blockchain ideas among ~10 in 2017 but rejected them because the tech could not scale; maturation of ZK technology is what made a decentralized, verifiable exchange at scale feasible later.
insights.speaker: Vlad (Lighter founder)
insights.so_what: ZK maturity was the gating enabler for on-chain order books; infra readiness, not first-mover status, determined winners.
insights.quote: ZK uh technologies really matured and we realized that that can actually be used to like run an exchange in a decentralized verifiable way at scale

insights.claim: Vlad says Lighter's timing was nearly optimal and at most he would have started about six months earlier; starting in 2017 would have failed on both immature tech and an unclear regulatory regime.
insights.speaker: Vlad (Lighter founder)
insights.so_what: Second-wave builders in crypto benefit from matured infra and regulatory clarity; first movers bear wasted costs.
insights.quote: maybe in like if we could go back in time, we would have started like six months earlier or something, but not more than that

insights.claim: Lighter's core technology is a general on-chain order book that can spin up any market with TradFi-like low latency and low cost while being verifiable, secure and composable; perps are just the first product.
insights.speaker: Vlad (Lighter founder)
insights.so_what: Lighter positions as market infrastructure, not a single perp DEX — TAM argument extends to all order-book markets.
insights.quote: we can spin up any market on chain with an order book and do it in the same low latency and lowcost um you know regime as as Stratfi while being verifiable and secure composable

insights.claim: Lighter's founders came out of an internal 'YC-style' process: about 6 months testing three ideas within the team, from which Lighter won.
insights.speaker: Vlad (Lighter founder)
insights.so_what: Founding team is technology-agnostic serial builders (former co-founder now at Cognition), not crypto-native ideologues.

insights.claim: Early perp DEX projects wasted effort on 'decentralization theater' to guess what regulators wanted, whereas today DC articulates core principles (security, verifiability, order matching, risk) enabling real conversations with regulators.
insights.speaker: Vlad (Lighter founder)
insights.so_what: Regulatory clarity now rewards substantive security/verifiability over cosmetic decentralization.
insights.quote: decentralization theater like oh let's try to make this feel more decentralized in hopes that that's what regulators want, but that's not actually the thing

insights.claim: Lighter is actively pursuing a CFTC license to operate in the US, listed alongside options and RWA liquidity as current top execution priorities.
insights.speaker: Vlad (Lighter founder)
insights.so_what: A CFTC-licensed on-chain perp venue would open the US market that most perp DEXs currently exclude.
insights.quote: getting the CFTC licensed operate in the US like those like we're very focused on that right now

insights.claim: At the CFTC innovation advisory committee meeting, with crypto firms and legacy firms present, Vlad reports broad consensus that 'the train has left the station' on the technology.
insights.speaker: Vlad (Lighter founder)
insights.so_what: Legacy finance and regulators converging on acceptance of on-chain market structure lowers adoption risk.
insights.quote: there's like pretty broad consensus that you know we're the train has left the station when it comes to technology

insights.claim: Traders care first about speed and UX; if a venue is unusable (high gas fees, ~10-second order delays as in 2021-2022), decentralization and trust assumptions do not matter to them.
insights.speaker: Vlad (Lighter founder)
insights.so_what: On-chain venues win on latency and cost parity with CEXs, not ideology.
insights.quote: traders really care about like speed and like good UX and so if you don't have that then all these other things like decentralization or trust assumptions like don't really matter

insights.claim: A venue must work well from day one because traders whose first experience is poor will not return later after latency or UX improvements.
insights.speaker: Vlad (Lighter founder)
insights.so_what: First-impression risk argues against shipping secure-but-slow MVPs in trading infra.
insights.quote: if that's their first experience, they're not going to come back later when you like improve the latency or improve the UX

insights.claim: Vlad observes that the on-chain trading products with the most adoption in the recent cycle were all started by founders with a trading background, unlike the earlier wave.
insights.speaker: Vlad (Lighter founder)
insights.so_what: Founder background (ex-traders) is a useful screening signal for evaluating perp DEX projects.
insights.quote: the products that have gained the most adoption I think were all started by kind of founders with a trading background

insights.claim: Lighter initially planned to launch spot first and add perps later, but flipped the order near launch; it started with perpetuals, added spot, and is now preparing to add options.
insights.speaker: Vlad (Lighter founder)
insights.so_what: Options launch is a near-term product catalyst; perps-first sequencing chosen for customer demand.
insights.quote: started with perpetuals and adding spotlight. Now we're getting ready to add options too

insights.claim: Vlad says crypto ideals still matter and users of decentralized rails need to buy into them, but capital will not be deposited at scale if latency turns good trades into losing trades.
insights.speaker: Vlad (Lighter founder)
insights.so_what: Both ideology and performance are necessary; neither alone is sufficient.

insights.claim: Lighter's zero-fee-for-retail model, charging professional traders, market makers and institutions instead, is borrowed from Robinhood, where Vlad was an early adviser about 12 years earlier.
insights.speaker: Vlad (Lighter founder)
insights.so_what: Lighter imports a proven TradFi payment-for-flow-style monetization into crypto.
insights.quote: I was early adviser to Robin Hood like 12 years prior

insights.claim: Vlad argues crypto lagged TradFi on fee structure: most of TradFi has adopted zero-cost retail with professional-side charging, while crypto had not.
insights.speaker: Vlad (Lighter founder)
insights.so_what: Fee compression for retail on crypto venues is likely to spread, pressuring venues reliant on retail taker fees.
insights.quote: that's actually in one area where like the crypto space was behind trfy

insights.claim: Retail is the hardest segment to attract because professionals participate wherever P&L exists while retail picks one venue with the best experience and won't run desks on 10 venues, so venues should remove all retail friction.
insights.speaker: Vlad (Lighter founder)
insights.so_what: Retail acquisition is the binding constraint; liquidity providers follow retail flow.
insights.quote: retail is the hardest part of the market to attract

insights.claim: Lighter ran points even for testnet beta traders, and its testnet-to-mainnet conversion rate was almost 100%.
insights.speaker: Vlad (Lighter founder)
insights.so_what: Rewarding testnet users can lock in sticky early liquidity before mainnet.
insights.quote: our conversion rate from testn net to mainet was like almost 100%

insights.claim: A points/token program is needed because traders face unknown unknowns moving to a new venue; token structure aligns builders, investors and early traders as owners.
insights.speaker: Vlad (Lighter founder)
insights.so_what: Token incentives function as risk compensation for venue switching, not just marketing.

insights.claim: Wash trading is harmful, not neutral: unhealthy volume relative to open interest deters serious traders evaluating a platform, so small wash traders can keep whales away.
insights.speaker: Vlad (Lighter founder)
insights.so_what: Volume/OI ratio is a key health metric; inflated volume can be a negative signal for perp DEXs.
insights.quote: small you know fish like doing watch trading might actually detract the big whale from coming in

insights.claim: Lighter's season 2 points formula was redesigned using season 1 data to penalize unhelpful behavior like wash trading and uses algorithmic cluster detection against Sybil clusters, while keeping the formula secret to prevent gaming.
insights.speaker: Vlad (Lighter founder)
insights.so_what: Points formulas evolving toward 'natural trading' reduce farmer ROI and improve market quality.
insights.quote: just trade how you would normally trade

insights.claim: Lighter's core bet is that most of finance moves on-chain, with Ethereum as the secure asset base layer and Lighter targeting the trading/market-operation layer above it with shared, capital-efficient balance sheets.
insights.speaker: Vlad (Lighter founder)
insights.so_what: Lighter positions as an Ethereum-aligned trading layer, a bullish read for Ethereum as settlement layer.
insights.quote: most of finance is going to move on chain

insights.claim: Vlad predicts on-chain markets, currently a very small part of global finance, can grow about 100x, and in 10 years a large part of global markets could run on Lighter tech directly or via partnerships like Robinhood's.
insights.speaker: Vlad (Lighter founder)
insights.so_what: Implies large TAM expansion for on-chain venues; Robinhood partnership is a distribution channel.
insights.quote: right now onchain markets are still a very small part of the financial ecosystem in the world. So there's like I think >> that can grow you know 100x

insights.claim: Vlad says Lighter at scale can be as massive as the next OpenAI or Anthropic, while acknowledging the thesis could be right but Lighter's market share smaller than hoped.
insights.speaker: Vlad (Lighter founder)
insights.so_what: Founder ambition is maximalist; execution and share risk acknowledged.
insights.quote: can be as massive as like you know I don't know the next open AI or anthropic

insights.claim: Lighter's current priorities are building options, improving liquidity on RWAs and obtaining a CFTC license; it explicitly does not set long-range targets like $100B daily volume, citing Jensen Huang's focus on today's plan.
insights.speaker: Vlad (Lighter founder)
insights.so_what: Near-term catalysts to track: options launch, RWA liquidity, CFTC licensing.

insights.claim: Fixed income traded on Lighter rails is cited as an untouched opportunity whose size (10B or 100B) Vlad says is unknown.
insights.speaker: Vlad (Lighter founder)
insights.so_what: On-chain fixed income is a potential next frontier after perps/spot/options.
insights.quote: we haven't even scratched the surface of fixed income

insights.claim: Vlad says most TradFi institutions have broadly embraced on-chain markets, with only a small minority still resisting entirely.
insights.speaker: Vlad (Lighter founder)
insights.so_what: Incumbent resistance is no longer the main adoption barrier.
insights.quote: there's maybe like like a small minority of tried five folks that are just resisting this uh innovation alto together but it's it's a small minority now

insights.claim: TradFi incumbents fall into three tiers: those chasing new crypto revenue streams, those tokenizing existing assets for wider distribution, and the best partners who build new products only possible on-chain (e.g. reimagined corporate actions, custody and settlement).
insights.speaker: Vlad (Lighter founder)
insights.so_what: Partnerships with incumbents building native on-chain products are the highest-value; pure tokenization is shallower.

insights.claim: Long-term focus and deeper technical understanding at a TradFi partner make for stronger partnerships with Lighter.
insights.speaker: Vlad (Lighter founder)
insights.so_what: Partner quality depends on time horizon and tech depth.
